headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading error: MinerU’s offline document ingestion can feed sensitive content into next-ai-draw-io’s broad cloud/model egress and MCP surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU can ingest local PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX and expose results via MCP; next-ai-draw-io also uses MCP and natural-language commands. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if MinerU output or shared files are treated as trusted input. The pairwise pathway is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly observed.
conditions: IF MinerU output is copied into next-ai-draw-io prompts or MCP messages, injection is possible.
IF either agent parses the other’s document text as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer behavior.
mitigations: Use a strict delimiter/template when passing text between agents.
Strip instructions from extracted documents before forwarding.
Disable MCP bridging between the two agents for untrusted content.
Review a sample handoff for prompt-like strings before production use.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU is documented as private/offline, but next-ai-draw-io has broad network egress to multiple third-party model APIs and handles API keys. If sensitive documents processed by MinerU are forwarded to next-ai-draw-io, the pair can exfiltrate document contents off-box by default. The risk is driven by the interaction of both agents’ documented surfaces.
conditions: IF MinerU outputs are sent into next-ai-draw-io for summarization or diagramming, sensitive text can leave the local environment.
IF next-ai-draw-io is configured to use a hosted model provider, document contents may be transmitted externally.
mitigations: Keep sensitive MinerU outputs out of next-ai-draw-io.
Force next-ai-draw-io to a local-only model path.
Redact secrets before any handoff.
Rotate any exposed API keys if documents may contain them.
requires-engineering: add an allowlist that blocks sensitive classes from reaching hosted APIs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support concurrent instances and MCP, and both can operate on document-like artifacts. Even without filesystem write permissions in MinerU, next-ai-draw-io’s broader network/model actions can conflict with shared mutable resources or shared MCP state if the orchestrator exposes them. The overlap is real but not proven to be destructive by default.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same MCP server or shared mutable workspace, concurrent updates can race.
IF the orchestrator grants shared OAuth or API credentials, one agent can overwrite or consume resources used by the other.
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces per agent.
Use distinct MCP servers or namespaces.
Serialize writes through the orchestrator.
Separate API keys and environment variables.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU is a document extractor whose outputs are likely to be treated as structured facts, while next-ai-draw-io is an AI-assisted visualization tool that can act on natural-language commands and external model outputs. If next-ai-draw-io consumes MinerU’s extracted text without verification, extraction errors or hallucinated structure can cascade into incorrect diagrams or actions.
conditions: IF MinerU extraction is used as authoritative input to next-ai-draw-io, errors propagate downstream.
IF next-ai-draw-io auto-generates diagrams or actions from extracted text without human review, the cascade becomes operational.
mitigations: Require human review before diagram generation.
Compare extracted fields against source documents.
Use confidence thresholds to gate handoff.
Log provenance from MinerU into next-ai-draw-io outputs.
requires-engineering: add validation rules for extracted schemas.

E_compliance.rationale: MinerU is described as private/offline, while next-ai-draw-io explicitly requests API keys and can send content to multiple external model providers. If regulated documents processed by MinerU are forwarded to next-ai-draw-io, retention, residency, and third-party processing obligations can diverge. The compliance gap is pairwise and depends on the chosen provider path.
conditions: IF EU PII or regulated documents are forwarded from MinerU to a hosted next-ai-draw-io provider, residency/compliance obligations may be violated.
IF retention policies differ between the local MinerU workflow and the hosted model provider, subject-rights handling can diverge.
mitigations: Keep regulated data local to MinerU.
Select a provider with matching compliance terms.
Document retention and deletion paths.
Avoid sending secrets or PHI through next-ai-draw-io.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class.
